env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# The elements of a tuple literal keep their whole text when they end in
# a call, an index, a slice, a parenthesis, a string holding closers or a
# raw string over two lines, and the literal keeps its own parentheses
# when it is wrapped in more. The module runs natively, ejects, and the
# ejected module builds and runs with go and with go1.27.2 from
# $UPROOT1272 and prints the same output.
cd m
logos run .
stdout '^1 2 2 3 1 3 \) \)\}// 4 3 5 6 9 10 7 8$'
cp stdout $WORK/native.txt
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
exists $UPROOT1272/bin/go
exec $UPROOT1272/bin/go version
stdout '^go version go1\.27\.2 '
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build -o $WORK/upstream$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/upstream$GOEXE
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
cd ..

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/tupleelems

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

type P struct{ X, Y int }

func id(n int) int {
	return n
}

func ret() (int, int) {
	return (id(9), id(10))
}

func wrapped() (int, int) {
	return ((7, 8))
}

func main() {
	xs := []int{1, 2, 3}
	a, b := (id(1), id(2))
	c, d := (xs[1], xs[2:][0])
	e, f := (P{1, 2}.X, (id(3)))
	g, h := (")", ")}//")
	i, j := (id(id(4)), `r
)`)
	k, l := ((5, 6))
	m, n := ret()
	o, p := wrapped()
	fmt.Println(a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, len(j), k, l, m, n, o, p)
}
